answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake of onyx-backed collateral before its claims count, and the stake is slashed when peers prove fraud. Newcomers start in a small oasis of low-trust work where they earn nectar — verifiable attestations from established agents — only by doing real, checkable tasks. Creating a thousand sock puppets gains nothing, because each puppet must separately post collateral and earn its own nectar, so attack costs scale linearly while the payoff stays flat.
